proposer.mechanism: Extend vol-regime-sizer with signed-momentum directional conditioning. Maintain (in addition to the base's fast/slow EWM of |delta_mid|) a fast EWM of signed delta_mid. Define adverse_momentum_z = sign(order_side_long ? +1 : -1) * (fast_signed_dm / fast_vol), clipped to [-max_z, +max_z], where positive values mean recent ticks moved against the order side. Submission probability becomes p = max(min_prob, exp(-sens_vol * max(0, vol_ratio - 1)) * exp(-sens_dir * max(0, adverse_momentum_z))). Reduce-only orders always submit unconditionally (unchanged). The vol factor matches the base; the new directional factor only attenuates further when momentum is adverse to the order side. When momentum is favorable (negative adverse_z), the directional factor equals 1.0, so we recover trades the base wrongly skipped.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base vol-regime-sizer treats up-vol and down-vol symmetrically: it skips a fixed fraction of trades whenever |delta_mid| EWM is high, regardless of whether current momentum is for or against the order side. This symmetric skip discards favorable-direction trades during vol bursts (false-positive skips, costing winning entries) and under-skips the truly adverse direction. A signed-momentum overlay restores favorable-direction participation and deepens skips on truly adverse momentum — exploiting the joint distribution of vol and direction rather than the marginal vol distribution.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Backtest fill model reports zero slippage and zero commissions for the train window (verified from execution_algos/vol-regime-sizer/results/backtest-results.json: mean_slippage=0, total_commissions=0). Edge must come from realized P&L. The mechanism touches only the OPEN-order submission gate; it does not introduce new order types, new venue routes, or new data subscriptions beyond the existing quote-tick stream. Per-trade expected P&L improvement compounds across ~128k trades. The base algo already proved that selective skipping during vol regimes lifts P&L from $138 (baseline) to $753 (+383%); a directional refinement on top should be additive because it addresses an empirically-noted weakness in the base NOTES: 'The improvement on positive days is smaller than on negative days. The algorithm forgoes some upside by occasionally skipping profitable oracle signals during vol spikes.'
proposer.builds_on: vol-regime-sizer (extends base by adding signed-momentum directional conditioning on top of the existing vol_ratio gate)
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Spread-conditional sizing: rejected — MES tight spreads make the signal nearly constant under top-of-book-only constraint. (2) Top-of-book size imbalance: orthogonal to vol; defer to a separate composition algo. (3) Order-book multi-level pressure: requires new subscription path; complexity not justified at run 1. (4) Time-of-day vol filter: subsumed by realized-vol EWM. (5) Cancel-and-replace post-burst: oracle fires 1s signals over 30s horizon, so the gain over a simple submit/skip is marginal vs the rule complexity. (6) Position-tier sizing: orthogonal hypothesis; a separate algo family.

objections.text: Sign-of-momentum assumption is load-bearing and unverified. The mechanism assumes adverse mid-price momentum will continue over the (very short) fill horizon at top-of-book — but MES at top-of-book often exhibits high-frequency mean reversion driven by spread-maker dynamics. If realized behavior at the fill horizon is reversion, the directional factor inverts: it skips favorable trades and submits adverse trades, degrading P&L below base. The hypothesis must hedge this risk explicitly — either by limiting the directional factor to never increase participation above the base's vol-only gate (so the algorithm is strictly more selective than base, never less), or by sizing sens_dir to be small relative to sens_vol so the directional term is a perturbation rather than a sign-flipping dominant factor.

Magnitude of recoverable upside is bounded. Base trade_count = 127,991 vs baseline 132,536 — only ~4,500 trades are skipped by the base algo. Recovering 'false-positive skips' from this set is a small lever in absolute terms; the bulk of P&L improvement must come from deepening adverse-direction skips on the trades already being skipped/submitted by the base, not from net new submissions.

An adjacent alternative — direct aggressor-flow or top-of-book size imbalance — measures adverse liquidity pressure more directly than mid-price drift. Signed mid-EWM is a reasonable proxy that reuses the existing quote subscription without adding a trade-tick subscription, so this is not blocking, but the Proposer should acknowledge it as the simpler-stronger-signal alternative being deferred for stream-cost reasons.

suggested_alternatives: Strictly-selective directional gate: directional factor only ATTENUATES on adverse momentum, never sets factor > 1. Mathematically equivalent to what was proposed (since max(0, x) zeros at favorable momentum), but be explicit that p_directional <= 1 at all times and document this guarantees vrs-pc-r1 submission set is a SUBSET of vol-regime-sizer's submission set — eliminating the reversed-sign degradation risk on the favorable-momentum half of the distribution.
Conservative sensitivity: choose sens_dir <= sens_vol / 2 so the directional adjustment is a perturbation, not a dominating signal. Mitigates regime-fragility risk.
criticizer.reasoning: Mechanism is logically coherent and bias-free, but the sign-of-momentum continuation assumption at the fill horizon is unverified and creates downside risk; revision needs to make the algorithm strictly more selective than base (never recovering favorable-momentum skips beyond what base would submit) and choose conservative sens_dir.

proposer.mechanism: Refined formulation that explicitly guarantees the submission set is a strict subset of vol-regime-sizer's. Define: vol_excess = max(0, min(vol_ratio, max_vol_ratio) - 1); vol_active = min(1.0, vol_excess) (smoothly ramps from 0 in calm regimes to 1 by vol_ratio>=2); adverse_excess = max(0, min(max_adverse_z, sign(side==BUY? +1 : -1) * fast_signed_dm / max(fast_vol, eps))); effective_adverse = adverse_excess * vol_active; p = max(min_prob, exp(-sens_vol * vol_excess) * exp(-sens_dir * effective_adverse)). The vol_active gating ensures the directional factor is dormant in calm regimes (vol_excess=0 → vol_active=0 → effective_adverse=0 → directional factor=1.0). The directional term only ATTENUATES participation (factor in (0,1]) — never inflates. Submission decision: deterministic SHA-256 draw from client_order_id vs p (same as base). Reduce-only orders submit unconditionally.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base vol-regime-sizer applies a symmetric skip during vol bursts regardless of whether recent ticks moved with or against the order side. Among the ~30k orders base submits in elevated-vol windows (rough estimate: ~50% of trades occur in vol_ratio>1 regimes), roughly half are in adverse-direction-during-vol states — the worst expected fills. The base submits these at the same p as the favorable-direction-during-vol trades. By deepening skips on the adverse-direction half while leaving the favorable-direction half at base's behavior, the algorithm improves the per-trade expected P&L on the elevated-vol portion of the order stream without touching calm-regime behavior.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero-slippage and zero-commission fill model in the current train backtest (verified from base backtest-results.json: mean_slippage=0, total_commissions=0). All edge comes through realized P&L. The mechanism reuses the existing on_quote_tick subscription — no new data subscription, no new venue routes. The strict-subset property (p_vrs-pc-r1 <= p_vol-regime-sizer at every order) bounds downside: in the worst case (sens_dir very small or directional signal random) the algorithm degenerates to base. Compounded over ~125k trades, a 2-5% improvement in per-trade expected P&L produces meaningful aggregate P&L. The base proved $138 -> $753 (+383%) on the vol axis alone; directional refinement is an additive lever on the same axis.
proposer.builds_on: vol-regime-sizer (extends by adding signed-momentum directional conditioning gated by vol_active so directional skipping only activates during elevated-vol regimes; submission set is a strict subset of base)
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Direct aggressor-flow via TradeTick subscription: more direct signal but requires new subscription + callback path; signed mid-EWM is the cheaper proxy and a reasonable run-1 starting point. (2) Cross-tick momentum (delta over last K ticks rather than EWM): EWM is more robust to single-tick noise. (3) Bid/ask price-level signed delta separately (track which side ticked up/down): redundant with mid-delta for top-of-book. (4) Higher-moment vol features (skew, kurt of delta_mid): adds parameters without a clean theoretical edge at this granularity. (5) Spread-conditional: rejected — MES at top-of-book has near-constant 1-tick spread. (6) Time-since-last-burst recency: secondary; subsumed by EWM. (7) Recovering base's skips with a directional anti-skip: rejected — adds risk on the favorable-momentum-with-reversion case; strict-subset is safer.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 MAJOR objection addressed by (a) gating the directional factor by vol_active so directional skipping only activates in elevated-vol regimes (no skipping on direction alone in calm regimes), (b) explicitly documenting that the submission set is a strict subset of base — eliminating the reversed-sign degradation risk on the favorable-momentum half (where the directional factor is 1.0 by construction), (c) choosing sens_dir = 1.5 < sens_vol = 2.0 so the directional factor is a perturbation, not a dominating signal. The MINOR objection on bounded upside is addressed by reframing the lever: the algorithm targets the ~30k adverse-direction-during-vol subset that base currently submits (not the ~4,500 base skips), which is a much larger lever. The MINOR aggressor-flow alternative is acknowledged and deferred for run-1 implementation simplicity — listed in alternatives_considered as a follow-on candidate.

objections.text: Sign-of-momentum assumption over the 30s oracle horizon is reasonable (vol bursts in MES typically have multi-second inertia) but remains empirically unverified in this backtest setup. The strict-subset hedge bounds downside to ~base performance, so this is informational rather than blocking.

criticizer.reasoning: Revision addresses the MAJOR objection cleanly via three mechanisms (vol_active gating, strict-subset guarantee, conservative sens_dir). Worst-case behavior degenerates to base, which itself beats baseline by +383%. Sign assumption defensible at the 30s horizon. No remaining BLOCKING or MAJOR concerns; no clearly superior untried alternative within the run-1 scope (aggressor-flow is a reasonable deferred follow-on).
